purpose: Curated machine-readable catalogue of real upstream agent repositories used as implementation references. Not project status, memory, or runtime authority.

references.name: OpenAI Codex
references.adopt: Separation of model-authored messages from runtime/tool/approval/completion state.
references.avoid: Do not copy the complete runtime when only a lifecycle or execution-boundary pattern is needed.

references.name: Cline
references.adopt: Centralized provider/model result semantics, host-owned runtime construction, and explicit team/session lifecycle.
references.avoid: Do not create a second provider subsystem when the target already has one canonical owner.

references.name: Hermes Agent
references.adopt: One agent core across channels, persistent turn orchestration, and progressive loading of memory, skills, and integrations.
references.avoid: Do not let gateway, memory, skills, or delegated work become a second untracked authority. Preserve working team/subagent features but keep parent/session ownership explicit.

references.name: OpenHands Agent Canvas
references.adopt: Use for the user-facing control-center boundary, backend selection, and client orchestration.
references.avoid: Do not treat OpenHands/OpenHands as the canonical agent/tool/conversation/workspace runtime owner; those implementations live in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk.

references.name: OpenHands software-agent-sdk
references.adopt: Use as the canonical OpenHands implementation reference for agents, tools, conversations, workspaces, events, security/confirmation, and the Agent Server API.
references.avoid: Do not confuse Agent Canvas frontend behavior with this runtime owner, and do not import the complete runtime when only a narrow action/observation or workspace contract is needed.

references.name: Aider
references.adopt: Repository mapping and selective context expansion before edits.
references.avoid: Do not equate repository awareness with file authority or load the whole repository into context.

references.name: LobeHub
references.adopt: Separate provider/model metadata, configuration, capability, readiness, and integration lifecycle.
references.avoid: Do not treat configured state as runtime readiness.

references.name: OpenClaw
references.adopt: Keep session/agent identity independent from CLI, UI, browser, or messaging transports.
references.avoid: Do not let channel clients become separate reasoning authorities.

references.name: Agent Zero
references.adopt: Use as a comparative implementation reference for extensibility and local-agent patterns.
references.avoid: Do not treat it as a default target architecture without checking ownership and lifecycle fit.

references.name: Gemini CLI
references.adopt: Use the browser-agent definition/factory/invocation/manager chain for browser-specialized agents, and the scheduler/policy/confirmation chain for tool execution.
references.avoid: Do not copy Gemini-specific model assumptions into provider-neutral layers; preserve the architectural seams rather than provider-specific defaults.

references.name: DeepSeek Harness
references.adopt: Use explicit package/service seams for the agent loop, ordered tool scheduling, browser/computer capability registration, subagent lifecycle, and skills.
references.avoid: Do not treat every plugin seam as a reason to fragment an existing target owner. Use the harness to make ownership explicit, not to create duplicate authority.
